text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore shares staged their biggest one-day rally so far this year, with the Straits Times Index climbing 35.27 points, or 1.7 percent, to 2,101.48.
- Mainboard-listed CAM International Holdings has appointed two key executives of a Malaysian subsidiary to take charge of the group's daily operations.
- Following a failed attempt in 1994, United Overseas Bank could be making a second bid to merge Far Eastern Bank with another bank in its stable.
- Japanese authorities, who just last week were talking down the U.S. dollar, shifted gears in an apparent effort to keep the dollar from sliding too far.
- Contrary to public perception, the Goods and Services Tax is no money spinner, with the government giving out more in refunds and related tax relief than it collects.
- One year after the government's surprise curbs against prpoerty speculation, HDB upgraders hold the key to a market that is subdued but stable.
- The U.S. dollar appeared to stabilise after a precipitous fall that seemed to be getting out of hand until senior Japanese officials stepped in to declare the decline has gone far enough.
- DBS Land subsidiary Australand will raise Singapore $167.54 million from its dual listing in Sydney and Singapore to fund its expansion plans.
- Hongkong-based parent of Elec and Eltek International Company is paring its stake from 65.39 percent to 51.8 percent in a share placement expected to raise over Singapore $100 million.
- IPCO International's Managing Director Charles Hardeman announced his resignation in what he said was a "mutual agreement" between him and IPCO's new shareholders, Promet Bhd.
- Showpla Asia Ltd looks set to be first company to list on the newly created foreign section of the Osaka Securities Exchange.
- Equipment supplier Poh Lian Holding's placement tranche of 8.1 million shares from its initial public offering has been fully subscribed. IPO managers United Overseas Bank said..
